rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for a person who travels from place to place without implying that they are Romani.

example.english: They are a gypsy who travels around and finds work wherever they go.
example.traditional: 佢成日周圍走嘅人，去到邊就喺邊度搵工。
example.jyutping: keoi5 seng4 jat6 zau1 wai4 zau2 ge3 jan4 heoi3 dou3 bin1 zau6 hai2 bin1 dou6 wan2 gung1

rows.note: Use this when the person is portrayed as homeless or living by wandering rather than simply travelling.

example.english: That gypsy often sleeps outside the station at night.
example.traditional: 嗰個流浪漢夜晚成日瞓喺車站門口。
example.jyutping: go2 go3 lau4 long6 hon3 je6 maan5 seng4 jat6 fan3 hai2 ce1 zaam6 mun4 hau2

rows.note: Use this for the old-fashioned itinerant-trader or travelling-performer side of the meaning.

example.english: A gypsy used to travel around selling knives and scissors, making a living by the gift of the gab.
example.traditional: 以前有個江湖客周圍去賣刀剪，靠口才搵食。
example.jyutping: ji5 cin4 jau5 go3 gong1 wu4 haak3 zau1 wai4 heoi3 maai6 dou1 zin2 kaau3 hau2 coi4 wan2 sik6
